units: milliseconds relative to post-Google workspace navigation start unless otherwise stated
method: Three fresh Google client logins with the same benchmark Google account and live build.

Sign out to the sign-in page; select Web Inspector Console and verify the reported focused UI is Console prompt before each console command. Clear localStorage and sessionStorage and verify both key lists are empty.

Keep Web Inspector open throughout. After workspace rendering, collect full navigation.toJSON(), paint entries, all mark entries, and every Resource Timing entry with full timing/size/serverTiming fields.
Export collected JSON using a Blob download from the confirmed Inspector console. Downloads are local benchmark files; no application records were changed.

Run 1 only: enable Screenshots, Network, Layout & Rendering, JavaScript & Events, CPU; keep Stop recording once page loads unchecked; start manual recording before selecting the Google account; export the resulting recording.

cache.interpretation: Zero-transfer, zero-body entries and short durations are consistent with cached/preloaded reuse. Positive transfer sizes are browser-reported network transfers. Cache was not cleared or disabled.
Zero-transfer, zero-body entries and short durations are consistent with cached/preloaded reuse. Positive transfer sizes are browser-reported network transfers. Cache was not cleared or disabled.
Zero-transfer, zero-body entries and short durations are consistent with cached/preloaded reuse. Positive transfer sizes are browser-reported network transfers. Cache was not cleared or disabled.

measuredFindings: All three runs have 171 Resource Timing entries, below the default 250-entry buffer limit, with 164 /assets/ entries and 68 beginning before /api/web/tokens.

All three runs show mixed cache use: 67 zero-transfer asset entries and 97 positive-transfer asset entries. Main stylesheet and workspace JavaScript have zero-transfer entries; entry script has a positive transfer size.
Safari exposed FCP but no separate first-paint entry in any run. Missing first-paint is stored as null.
Redirect intervals were 732, 761, and 709 ms. Request-to-first-byte intervals were 649, 187, and 207 ms.
Run 1 HTML serverTiming reports app=594.6 ms and db=583 ms; runs 2/3 report app=144/167.2 ms and db=124.7/145.6 ms. HTML reports queries=6 in all three runs.
Web token durations were 469, 216, and 164 ms. The corresponding server app timings were 414.7, 169.4, and 126.3 ms; DB timings were 374, 147.7, and 94 ms (queries=3).
inferences: Run 1 has substantially longer server-side application/DB timing than runs 2/3, consistent with much of its extra response latency being server-side. This does not identify the cause of DB variability.

A cached workspace chunk responseEnd is a fetch/reuse timing, not the end of JavaScript execution. The workspace-code mark is the available completion mark. Missing Timelines events prevent attribution of the gap to parsing, evaluation, scheduling, or rendering.

limitations: Manual recording was started on the Google chooser before selecting the account. It stopped/replaced itself during the Google return despite page-load auto-stop being unchecked.

The export ends at 1666 ms, before Navigation Timing FCP at 1702 ms and workspace-code at 2146 ms. Markers for DOMContentLoaded/load exist after the last recorded events; they do not establish complete script/layout capture.
Screenshots were enabled but no screenshot records were exported. Splash/workspace screenshot times cannot be measured.
Only two script-evaluated events were exported, with no source URL or function attribution. They are not claimed to be the five longest startup tasks.
No layout/style event over 50 ms appears in the captured interval; the missing interval prevents a claim about the whole startup.
Export timestamps use the Inspector clock, which was not independently aligned to Navigation Timing.

limits: These are three observations with mixed browser cache state. Application storage was cleared, browser HTTP cache and Google session were retained.
Google account-choice time is excluded. Navigation Timing includes the exposed post-Google redirect interval.
The sign-in return targets were draft routes inherited from the benchmark window, recorded in nav.name; all runs opened the same draft workspace UI.
No composer-ready marker was exposed. Workspace rendering and host-ready do not independently establish every control being usable.
The Timelines export is incomplete, so requested full-load screenshot/task/per-script/layout findings remain unavailable.
